sentences.text: Linhevenator possessed sickle-claws and raptorial hands, features typical of troodontids, along with a second toe carrying a large claw larger than those found in basal relatives.
As troodontids, Linhevenator possessed high encephalization quotients indicating advanced behavior and keen senses.
The species Linhevenator tani was named and described in 2011 by Xu Xing, Tan Qingwei, Corwin Sullivan, Han Fenglu, and Xiao Dong.
Linhevenator was classified as a derived troodontid in a phylogenetic analysis, appearing in a polytomy with Troodon and a clade containing Zanabazar and Saurornithoides.
Linhevenator lived during the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) in the Bayan Mandahu Formation of Bayan Mandahu, Inner Mongolia, China, approximately 75 million years ago.
